novelty_flags.label: Theorem thm:causal-functional
novelty_flags.one_line: Its displayed ratio is the population counterpart of Moreau-Kastler's equation (3.14); retain it only as a setup definition or sanity reduction, not a novel root theorem.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition prop:homogeneous-known-mass-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: Once the baseline mass is known and treatment is homogeneous, this is the classical one-parameter Poisson-mean problem already treated by Kabaila and Byrne.

novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question oeq:uniform-certificate
novelty_flags.one_line: The asserted strict strengthening is only against SchaferStark2009; add a second named certification comparator or state a generic-class obstruction before presenting this seed as flagship-grade.

novelty_flags.label: Open-ended Question oeq:uniform-certificate
novelty_flags.one_line: The claim to strictly strengthen SchaferStark2009 is not formalized as a theorem-level separation between its finite-prior approximation guarantee and the proposed certificate guarantee.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem thm:causal-functional
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed equality is obtained solely by substituting the definitions of H, B, w, and theta; move it to setup unless a nontrivial observed-law identification argument is added.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question oeq:uniform-certificate
soundness_flags.one_line: A terminating algorithm cannot literally return an unspecified Borel family; specify a finite machine representation of kappa-to-policy maps, exact input encoding, and the verifier's acceptance predicate.

soundness_flags.label: ass:exposure-box, ass:time-box, ass:treated-multiplier-box
soundness_flags.one_line: EvansHansenStark2005 studies restricted location parameters and bounded normal means, not these particular multiplicative-panel boxes as a standard condition; retag them as maintained restrictions and justify the calibration.

soundness_flags.label: ass:known-intensity
soundness_flags.one_line: KabailaByrne2001 treats an unknown scalar Poisson expectation, so it does not support calling known kappa a standard Poisson-exposure condition; state why exposure intensity is known in the intended applications.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Model-wide exact-inference spine
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Independent product-Poisson totals, known intensity, share overlap, and compact nuisance boxes are maintained rather than consequences of PPML quasi-likelihood.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All exact minimax and certification claims are conditional on the declared finite product-Poisson experiment; this is accepted scope after the unsupported standard tags are corrected.

source_verification_receipts.version: EU Tax Observatory Working Paper 31, May 6 2025 version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Equation (3.14) defines the imputed proportional effect as the ratio of treated observed outcomes to treated counterfactual outcomes minus one and interprets it as the percentage change in the average outcome.
The article constructs an exact confidence interval for the expectation theta of a Poisson random variable, with increasing endpoints and a no-shortening property.

The paper concerns minimax expected-measure confidence sets for restricted location parameters and develops bounded-normal-mean examples; it does not establish the proposed multiplicative exposure, time-effect, or treatment-multiplier boxes as standard panel assumptions.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 104(487) (2009), pp. 1080-1089
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives Monte Carlo approximation to a finite-prior minimax procedure; Theorem 6 bounds risk through Z(theta), and the conclusion states almost-sure convergence of maximum numerical risk to the finite-prior minimax risk.
Under index parallel trends, the paper identifies staggered cohort-time ATTs and states that canonical-link pooled quasi-likelihood and imputation produce identical estimates.
The paper states that a class of fixed-effect averages in multiplicative unobserved-effects panels is consistent and asymptotically normal with only the cross section growing.
The paper establishes global asymptotic equivalence between a variable-intensity Poisson process and Gaussian white noise under smoothness conditions, using explicit equivalence mappings.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Move thm:causal-functional and prop:homogeneous-known-mass-reduction into setup/sanity material, and reserve root targets for the nontrivial minimax, certification, and bridge claims.
Define the certificate output as finite code for piecewise policy maps with rational enclosure data, a verifier predicate, and a worked T=3 certification instance satisfying the stated .05 gap test.

Retag the compact boxes and known-intensity condition as explicit maintained restrictions, give a substantive exposure-design justification, and add an unknown-intensity or estimated-exposure extension as a clearly separated attainable regime.

Make the certificate theorem formally dominate two published computational approaches, or prove a generic impossibility/insufficiency result for finite-prior simulation certificates, to clear the comparator-chain flagship floor.

recommended_next_step: Continue revision: formalize the certificate's computable output and comparator separation, correct the assumption tags, and demote the two known/definitional root statements before Stage 0.
